detail: Later Sheffield history dates Pitchford’s initial idea to this month.
Pitchford proposes a psychiatry and abnormal-psychology forum on BIONET.
Price points to an existing newsgroup; Davis expresses interest.
The unmoderated psychiatry@mailbase.ac.uk list is announced.
March founding appears in Figley’s later CV; an April public announcement survives.
First newsletter records the board’s naming decision; PsychNet wording persists.
Eight lists grow from 1,993 to 2,250 subscriptions; figures overlap across people.
The newsletter estimates its total distribution, through redistribution lists, at more than 10,000.
An update reports more than 2,500 members and lists the forums and board.
A volunteer team takes over production after Pitchford’s first three issues.
Psychoanalysis, forensic psychiatry, emergency psychiatry and current-issues lists are announced.
Benjamin Goldhagen, later named executive director, seeks a newsletter section editor and says InterPsych engages over 4,000 people.
A call goes out for volunteers to gather data for the InterPsych Virtual Campus.
Pitchford appeals over the loss of Mailbase support.
The newsletter’s request for editors and contributors is forwarded to other lists.
Strategic Planning Committee, legal assistance and proposed campus are reported.
Rural-Care opens on a University of Helsinki Majordomo server; other new forums follow there.
A roster sets out forums, coordinators, directors and services, and claims more than 7,000 members.
A commercial interim host is chosen.
Pitchford, signing as Secretary of the Board, advertises volunteer director posts for clinical, research and education departments.
March newsletter reports the final end of Mailbase connections.
Joining guide distinguishes open groups from credentialed professional forums.
State records date the filing of INTERPSYCH, INC.
A sci.psychology reorganisation proposal cites the volume of InterPsych lists.
June report names InterPsych and the trauma forum as founding sponsors.
A forum listing names Seligman as President and Pitchford as Founder; Pitchford describes InterPsych as a non-profit registered in New York.
Robert G. White publicly calls for an elected president and board.
Pitchford announces EuroPsych, a confederation of societies, institutions and charities.
Young describes a confrontation and forum-leader settlement.
Plaud moves the clinical-psychologists list to North Dakota and reports Seligman’s resignation and the withdrawal of APA support.
The newsletter’s staff box drops the managing editor and its disclaimer drops the Board of Directors.
Assessment-Psychometrics reports moving independently to St John’s.
A notice of the GlobalPsych Institute site at Sheffield is relayed by Net-Happenings.
Pitchford announces charter discussions for a broader confederation.
A re-posted forum listing is headed only “Founded in 1994 by Ian Pitchford”.
Editorial history dates the decision to continue independently to this month.
Psychiatric Bulletin and American Journal of Psychiatry articles describe the network for clinicians.
First surviving issue and the independent Scout notice document the new title.
Pitchford joins the PsychNews staff as a consulting editor; the newsletter had stopped describing itself as associated with InterPsych in July.
Journal appears in the affiliated PsyCom.Net community, including Fisher’s forum essays.
New St John’s pages describe the multi-institutional consortium.
Pitchford advertises InterPsych as the world’s first and largest mental-health cyberorganization, with fifty lists and ten thousand members.
A compassion-fatigue poster draws 19 of its 179 respondents from InterPsych.
Figley’s editorial describes the InterPsych forum’s relationship to the journal.
Grohol discusses organisational limits; Dubovsky evaluates online consultation.
Zenhausern reports more than 45 affiliated lists.
Page footer dates an elected federation with autonomous forums.
Sheffield page names Greg Alter president, Dubovsky past president and Stamm president emeritus.
Seligman traces the APA e-journal Treatment to debates on InterPsych’s forums.
Archive captures preserve 44 forum pages naming coordinators and describing each forum.
A maintained page explains how new forums join the federation.
Forum leaders list 20 active forums serving over 5,000 professionals and record the 1998 purchase of interpsych.org.
Carbonell and Figley describe research nominations obtained through the network.
Bailey and Shriver recruit clinical psychologists through InterPsych’s clinical psychology list.
InterPsych.net directory includes revised entries in a 27-forum listing.
PsychNews reports that InterPsych’s main website is temporarily down; this is the latest dated organisational item found.
ISTSS still places two forums within InterPsych and names Figley president.
University directory and bylaws pages bear this date.
InterPsych-specific page update survives in a 2005 capture.
Education manuscript discusses InterPsych; BMJ editorial cites a newsletter item.
Digby Tantam declares that he had been a director of InterPsych.
InterPsych.net is parked by this capture; no organisational end date follows.
The corporation remains in the active-entity dataset; operational status is unresolved.
